newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, feeder cattle higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, feeder cattle higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed with June and August turning higher in fast late trading, while feeder cattle closed lower.

Traders said R.B.& H. and R.J. O'Brien were late buyers of June cattle that triggered local short covering and chart-based buying. The buying appeared to be largely technical because there was no apparent change in the cash cattle or beef markets to trigger it, traders said.

At midday, USDA reported beef cutout values were down another $0.69 to $0.23 per cwt. In the feedlot markets, a small amount of cattle traded at $65.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from top prices last week and early this week.
Speculative buying against light cash hedging was featured in the June contract, while hedge selling was active in the August, traders said.

Active placements since March should make for a large number of market-ready cattle available from July to August, traders said. However, they said feedlots have been selling cattle ahead of schedule which could somewhat pare down the July-August cattle supply.
Feeder cattle were pressured throughout the session by higher CBOT corn futures. CBOT corn was higher largely because the market was correcting from recent declines, CBOT traders said.
Live cattle closed up 0.500 cent per lb to down 0.450 cent with June up 0.500 at 65.400 cents. Feeder cattle were down 0.450 to 0.050 cent with August off the most at 78.450 cents.
